documents.title: THE LAW OF RESPONSIBLE HUMAN STEWARDSHIP
documents.abstract: Defines responsible human stewardship as the purpose governing the author's ecosystem. It places agency, continuity, legitimacy, accountability, and reality alignment above capability expansion as ends in themselves.
claims: Capability and execution may be delegated; stewardship and responsibility remain with humanity.
The source requires evidence and reality confirmation rather than intention alone for stewardship claims.
Downstream systems are presented as serving this governing purpose rather than existing as ends in themselves.
documents.boundary: Normative governance philosophy and ecosystem purpose; not an empirical demonstration of deployed systems.

documents.title: GOVERNING PRINCIPLES
documents.abstract: Sets out the foundational, structural, execution, and diagnostic principles used within the Governing Engines framework. It connects stable meaning and explicit authority to reviewable proof and governed continuation.
claims: The source organizes principles into four levels of operational governance.
Meaning, authority, validation, continuation, and proof are treated as linked stability requirements.
Derivative systems may specialize the principles but are instructed not to weaken proof, admissibility, or reviewability.
documents.boundary: Author-defined canonical rules within the Governing Engines ecosystem; no claim of authority over outside organizations or established universal law.

documents.title: CANONICAL TERMINOLOGY REGISTRY
documents.abstract: Defines continuity-governance vocabulary with allowed uses, prohibited interpretations, dependencies, and inheritance rules. Version 1.2 expressly supersedes 1.1 while preserving its historical lineage.
claims: Continuity is defined through preserved relationships among intent, interpretation, execution, consequence, memory, identity, and reality.
Execution correctness is distinguished from interpretation correctness.
Definitions include dependency and drift-risk information rather than labels alone.
documents.boundary: A terminology authority for the author's framework, not an independent validation of the underlying systems. Date is not stated in the supplied text.

documents.title: RUNTIME OBSERVATION REFINEMENT METHOD
documents.abstract: Describes an iterative construct, execute, observe, compare, diagnose, refine, validate, and repeat method. It uses actual runtime behavior to test whether implementation matches intended behavior.
claims: Specifications describe intended behavior while runtime supplies observations of actual behavior.
Observation does not automatically authorize modification; diagnosis and evidence-supported refinement come first.
A refinement must resolve the observed deficiency without degrading previously correct behavior.
documents.boundary: Draft engineering method; no comparative performance results or universal effectiveness demonstration are claimed.

documents.title: AI OPERATOR & SYSTEM BUILDER DEVELOPMENT FRAMEWORK
documents.abstract: Frames operator development around reasoning, interpretation, continuity, validation, and governed construction rather than tool familiarity alone. It situates operator capability within a lineage of governance and continuity work.
claims: Tool familiarity is distinguished from the capacity to govern and construct systems.
Execution coherence is not treated as proof of interpretation coherence.
Capability claims remain subject to reality-based validation rather than persistence or construction activity alone.
documents.boundary: Training and governance framework, not a measured training-effectiveness study.

documents.title: MODE PUBLIC BUILD SPECIFICATION
documents.abstract: Specifies a MODE-compatible runtime between human meaning and downstream execution. Its public contracts address interpretation, understanding, specification, context, memory, observation, and validation without requiring access to the private repository.
claims: Compatibility depends on governing contracts, not on naming a runtime MODE or adding an agent loop.
The specification forbids claims of execution without evidence that execution occurred.
Material unresolved meaning and semantic drift constrain promotion toward execution.
documents.boundary: Public core-runtime implementation specification; publication does not establish that a compatible implementation is integrated, validated, or operational. Creative-production and game-specific systems are outside scope.

documents.title: SPEC CLOUD
documents.subtitle: Unified Architecture, Governance Contracts, and Reference Implementation
documents.status: Specification-complete consolidated build authority; implementation state must be proven separately
documents.abstract: Consolidates Spec Cloud architecture, governance contracts, reference implementation specifications, and gap-closure rules. It makes material semantic and authority transitions versioned, attributable, and bound to evidence.
claims: Meaning mutation is expected; silent mutation is prohibited by the framework.
Specification completeness, implementation completeness, integration, validation, and operational deployment are distinct states.
The document states explicit supersession order and requires evidence before reporting an operational platform.
documents.boundary: Consolidated architecture and implementation authority, not proof that production code or a qualified deployment exists.

documents.title: OPERATOR GOVERNANCE COLLECTION
documents.abstract: Collects Operator Manual, Interpretation Integrity, Operator Isolation & Continuity Load, Recursive Discipline, Operator Capability Expansion, and Operator & User Relationship. Source-level status and lineage remain distinct within the compilation.
claims: The compilation preserves source-level wording and does not silently reconcile or supersede it.
Operator governance is treated as an upstream responsibility supporting downstream users.
Execution stability is distinguished from interpretation stability.
documents.boundary: A collection of governance frameworks; compilation is not empirical validation or implementation evidence.

documents.title: GOVERNED TEVV FOR AGENTIC AI
documents.subtitle: Architecture, Governance Authority, Operational Implementation, and Construction Method
documents.status: Official External Release — Architecture Locked / Frozen for External Handoff
documents.abstract: Presents a public construction package for a governed TEVV runtime, with concept, source of truth, governance authority, operational implementation, and technical build specification. The document describes its relationship to NIST evaluation work as a technical contribution.
claims: Action proposal, admissibility, authorization, execution, observation, and validation are separate functions.
An action proposal has no execution authority by itself.
The proposer may not author the authoritative success criteria for its own consequential action.
documents.boundary: Frozen construction package and author-described NIST-aligned contribution; not a claim of NIST endorsement, adoption, or production deployment.

documents.title: GOVERNED ADAPTIVE CONTROL FOR FAULT-TOLERANT QUANTUM SYSTEMS
documents.subtitle: Architecture and Operational Implementation Handoff
documents.status: Official External Release — Architecture and Operational Implementation Handoff
documents.abstract: Proposes governance domains around adaptive quantum control, separating evidence, interpretation, proposal, authority, execution, and validation. It leaves platform-specific realization and experimental determination to organizations with the necessary physical infrastructure.
claims: Proposal generation and execution authorization are separated in the proposed control architecture.
Domain separation constrains self-authorization and self-certification.
The handoff supplies falsification paths for a receiving technical organization to evaluate.
documents.boundary: The source expressly describes the architecture as an unvalidated proposal. Known quantum constraints do not validate the proposed architecture.

documents.title: AI DOOM
documents.subtitle: When Abstraction Outranks Reality
documents.version: Filename v1.2; cover Publication Edition v1.1
documents.abstract: Argues that AI can amplify institutional drift when abstractions retain authority despite contradictory reality. It frames AI Doom as a conditional failure trajectory rather than a prophecy and develops reality-coupled governance requirements.
claims: The thesis does not require malicious intent or inevitable catastrophe.
Increasing authority without adequate external validation and correction capacity is the hypothesized risk trajectory.
Diagnostic metrics are proposed structures rather than validated statistical indices.
documents.boundary: Conceptual systems thesis with bounded cited cases. Filename and cover version differ and are recorded without silently resolving the discrepancy.

documents.title: DANGER ZONES
documents.subtitle: PROOF BEFORE HARM BECOMES EVIDENCE
documents.abstract: Proposes a diagnostic decomposition for situations where capability, authority, value, or reliance outruns available proof. It organizes preventive governance around state dependency and evidence required to justify continuation.
claims: The six Danger Zones are proposed diagnostic categories, not proven natural categories.
The framework argues against making victims the monitoring layer.
Proof Burden Classes, the Ledger Rule, and worked-case evaluation are identified as the author's analytical contributions.
documents.boundary: Public research draft; the supplied practitioner corpus is non-random. Proposed rules and diagnostic categories must not be represented as empirically validated universals.

related_evidence.follow-the-harm: Research lineage and section 10 explicitly name Follow the Harm and define the companion relationship.

documents.title: BEFORE YOU NAME THE MACHINE
documents.subtitle: A Statement on Intelligence, Abstraction, Reality, and Civilizational Correction
documents.abstract: Traces a reality-first approach from personal observation and creation toward questions about intelligence, institutional correction, and AI. It distinguishes observation, interpretation, hypothesis, and open questions.
claims: Representations must be capable of revision when consequences contradict them.
The statement links observation, understanding, choice, action, consequence, and correction.
Cross-domain recurrence is treated as investigative evidence rather than proof of a universal law.
documents.boundary: Authorial statement with explicit evidence distinctions. It does not use the upstream OpenAI/Replit mechanism as a settled causal example.

related_evidence.the-passenger: The supplied statement explicitly cites The Passenger v1.2 and names its reality/consequence loop.

documents.title: SEMANTIC COMPRESSION
documents.subtitle: How Labels Hide Structure, Collapse Distinctions, and Obscure Reality
documents.abstract: Examines how useful compressed labels can become structurally misleading when material distinctions disappear. Version 1.4 includes scoped internal certification and contradiction-triggered revalidation rules.
claims: Compression is necessary infrastructure; the risk arises when a representation outranks the condition represented.
A linguistically true statement can omit distinctions material to authority, cost, classification, or proof.
Internal framework certification is scoped and reopenable rather than independent external certification.
documents.boundary: Analytical framework and internal certification protocol; not independent empirical certification, legal approval, or immunity from contradiction.

documents.title: THE ESCAPE ARTIST
documents.subtitle: Behavior, Authority, Containment, and Consequence in Agentic AI
documents.abstract: Separates concerning behavior from authority, containment, enforcement custody, and consequence. It treats controlled evaluations and real incidents according to their different evidentiary limits rather than collapsing them into a single escape narrative.
claims: Behavior, authority, containment, and consequence are distinct diagnostic variables.
Controlled evaluations can indicate behavioral disposition without proving failed production containment.
The paper does not establish one internal mechanism explaining all cases.
documents.boundary: Bounded incident analysis with a stated evidence cutoff and incomplete inquiry replay. Later Replit evidence is linked separately rather than silently inserted into this edition.

documents.title: THE SYSTEM DIDN'T WORK. THE OPERATOR DID.
documents.subtitle: How Workarounds Hide Failure While Proof Standards Keep Moving
documents.abstract: Examines how proxies and human compensation can make unreliable systems appear successful. It connects workarounds, proof requirements, capability visibility, and allocation through a proposed proxy-substitution mechanism.
claims: A completed task or successful-looking artifact need not establish reliable system execution.
The paper proposes Reliability Theater, Proof-Class Confusion, and Hidden Builder Burden as analytical concepts.
Evidence of workaround burdens does not establish their universal prevalence or the full proposed mechanism.
documents.boundary: Research draft distinguishing external empirical support from author-proposed mechanisms and governance rules. Prior Governing Engines papers are not treated as independent empirical proof.

documents.title: THE COST OF THE OUTCOME
documents.subtitle: Why AI Efficiency Must Be Measured at the System Boundary
documents.abstract: Proposes Total Cost to Valid Outcome as a measurement boundary for AI economics. It asks whether local generation savings persist after review, rework, integration, coordination, validation, and recovery costs are included.
claims: A faster local operation does not necessarily make the complete objective cheaper.
TCVO distinguishes cost elimination, cost reduction, and cost migration.
Comparisons require materially equivalent valid outcomes rather than output volume alone.
documents.boundary: Proposed conceptual measurement framework; does not estimate industry-wide savings/losses or claim all AI deployments exhibit cost migration.

documents.title: EXECUTIVE BRIEF — OPERATIONAL DRIFT GOVERNANCE AND GOVERNED EXECUTION INFRASTRUCTURE
documents.abstract: Describes operational instability as potentially originating in meaning, interpretation, authority, continuation, or proof before runtime. It presents governed operational infrastructure as an upstream enterprise-governance concern.
claims: The framework treats runtime failure as potentially downstream of earlier governance drift.
Meaning, interpretation, execution legitimacy, and continuation validity are distinct governance objects.
The document derives its vocabulary and authority relationships from the author's principles and terminology lineage.
documents.boundary: Executive framework, not an independently tested enterprise-outcome claim. References to terminology v1.1 remain source lineage; the supplied registry itself is v1.2.

documents.title: WHAT IS INTELLIGENCE?
documents.subtitle: A Reality-Primacy Investigation of Process, Compression, and State Change
documents.abstract: Investigates whether intelligence can be defined through consequential relationships compressed into operational form. It preserves the progression from conventional definitions through process, memory, learning, representation, and compression.
claims: The proposed working definition is explicitly a bounded hypothesis rather than established fact.
The inquiry tests definitions against reality instead of treating the definition as the phenomenon.
The source does not claim that Earth is conscious, rocks think, or all causation is intelligence.
documents.boundary: Conceptual investigation with prior-art references; those references do not prove its proposed definition. Filename and title-page versions differ.

documents.title: THE MASK AI RESEARCH WEARS
documents.subtitle: Human Inquiry, Machine Progression, and the Quiet Reassignment of the Researcher
documents.abstract: Investigates how AI can preserve the appearance of research artifacts while shifting the location of inquiry and human participation. It develops research-custody concepts and a bounded integrative architecture with explicit adjudication boundaries.
claims: A research artifact is distinct from the inquiry that produced it.
The paper narrows novelty claims where provenance, competing hypotheses, and revision have substantial prior art.
Version 1.2 separates detection/proposal of material changes from their adjudication.
documents.boundary: Analytical and architectural contribution with falsification conditions; not a claim that its proposed composite is deployed or uniquely invents all component mechanisms.

documents.title: PAST. PRESENT. FUTURE.
documents.subtitle: How Humanity Industrialized Representation — and What We Could Point Outward Next
documents.abstract: Compares historical technologies, recent technological forms, and reality-facing control examples to examine the direction of capability. It distinguishes documented purpose, demonstrated capability, architectural inference, and open possibility.
claims: The source rejects a simple history in which all technologies begin reality-facing and later become abstraction.
Demonstrated components do not establish a complete self-sustaining off-world research factory.
Physical outcomes must remain distinct from generated representations and corporate positioning.
documents.boundary: Comparative analysis and bounded architectural inference; no claim of AGI, unlimited autonomy, or an end-to-end demonstrated off-world inquiry system.

documents.title: BEFORE WE ARRIVE
documents.subtitle: A Persistent Architecture for Human Inquiry and Capability Beyond Earth
documents.abstract: Proposes persistent inquiry across temporary operators, institutions, embodiments, and distributed physical nodes. It separates constitutional authorization from factual truth and leaves succession and platform engineering questions open.
claims: The proposed contribution is governed integration, not invention of autonomous science or resource utilization.
Human amendment authority is expressed through a verifiable authority record rather than one prescribed technology.
Version 1.0 publication closure does not claim the complete architecture works.
documents.boundary: Architecture proposal; constitutional succession, end-to-end engineering, and experimental validation remain open.

documents.title: HUMAN ABSTRACTIONS
documents.subtitle: Remembering Which Rules Belong to the World and Which Rules Belong to Us
documents.abstract: Separates reality-bound responsibilities from the constructed mechanisms used to address them. It proposes a decomposition and removal test for assessing whether current institutional forms are necessary or merely consequential within an existing architecture.
claims: Real consequences do not by themselves establish reality-level necessity of an institution.
The removal test does not prove an alternative will work at scale.
The proposed categories remain revisable, and neither inherited institutions nor alternatives receive automatic validity.
documents.boundary: Analytical decomposition method with explicit unresolved states, not a proof that a proposed replacement architecture is feasible.

documents.title: CIVILIZATIONAL DRIFT
documents.subtitle: Convergence Emergence — Loss of Continuity — Directional Drift — Living Through Stagnation — Governance Rediscovery
documents.abstract: Assembles observations about continuity, direction, and governance across institutions and technology. It argues that AI accelerated visibility of existing continuity failures rather than creating all modern drift.
claims: The author presents the work as observation, not prophecy or AI evangelism.
Activity is distinguished from progress, and capability from direction.
The document preserves the emergence and lineage of its argument as unfinished work.
documents.boundary: Public observational synthesis; version and date are not explicitly stated in the supplied document and are not inferred from the filename.

documents.title: DESIGN THE ECOSYSTEM, NOT THE SUBSYSTEMS
documents.subtitle: A Systems Case for Restructuring the Architecture of American Social Life
documents.abstract: Examines how individually rational institutions can create incompatible conditions for households at their interfaces. It separates documented subsystem burdens from a stronger architectural hypothesis about interface-caused failure.
claims: A household experiences time, money, care, mobility, and eligibility as one interconnected environment.
Evidence of subsystem burdens does not by itself prove the magnitude of interface-caused household failure.
The proposed federated governance layer emphasizes observability, correction, and independent validation.
documents.boundary: The interface-failure hypothesis remains to be tested; the source marks some worked examples unresolved or illustrative-only rather than validated stress tests.

documents.title: SEED ADOPTION
documents.subtitle: When Does Technological Displacement Actually Begin?
documents.abstract: Examines how assistive adoption can create infrastructure and institutional positions that later substitution inherits. It distinguishes displacement potential from inevitability and differentiates sourced cases from illustrative mechanisms.
claims: Potential displacement can begin before a job-loss event becomes visible.
Assistive capability may establish infrastructure, legitimacy, data, or dependency for later substitution.
The source does not claim every useful technology eventually replaces its user.
documents.boundary: Analytical adoption framework; some examples are explicitly illustrations rather than evidence-based displacement claims.

documents.title: THE AMERICA THEY BUILT
documents.subtitle: A Generational Family-Viability Analysis, 1981–2026
documents.abstract: Compares modeled family basic-needs thresholds across historical and contemporary conditions, with a Franklin County, Ohio household example. It argues that judgments about choices should account for inherited economic constraints.
claims: The comparison distinguishes ordinary inflation from changes in the complete family cost structure.
Historical estimates use an explicitly modeled childcare proxy rather than a directly equivalent measured household.
The argument does not claim families in 1981 experienced no hardship.
documents.boundary: A geographically and methodologically bounded white paper with author calculations; historical modeled values are not universal household measurements.

documents.title: Economic Power, Political Spending, and Regulatory Conflict
documents.version: Filename v3; no internal version label identified
documents.status: Public-integrity brief; advocacy and policy analysis
documents.abstract: Examines whether existing conflict frameworks adequately address concentrated political spending, policy access, and government-dependent commercial interests. It explicitly separates structural concerns from findings of unlawful conduct.
claims: The brief does not allege an established campaign-finance violation, unlawful coordination, or a proven quid pro quo.
Access and economic exposure are analyzed as a potential governance conflict rather than proof of corruption.
Its reform argument is framed as capable of revision if the supporting structure is not established.
documents.boundary: Author advocacy and policy-analysis brief, not legal advice or a finding of unlawful conduct. External factual citations are source claims, not independently reverified by this catalog.

documents.title: EXECUTION WITHOUT AUTHORIZATION
documents.subtitle: A Replit Agent Billing & Control Case Study
documents.abstract: Reconstructs an operator-reported billing and execution-control incident using account notices and provider support statements. It asks whether restoration of eligibility was treated as authority for continued paid execution.
claims: The governing distinction is payment or billing eligibility versus fresh execution authority.
The source separates support explanations from unresolved task-level causal provenance.
It proposes execution-control and billing-review safeguards without claiming every disputed charge was finally adjudicated.
documents.boundary: Bounded incident account and control proposal. Historical provider explanations must be read alongside the later cross-system attribution update, not generalized to all incidents.

documents.title: EXECUTION WITHOUT PROVENANCE
documents.subtitle: A Replit Agent Post-Notice Execution, Billing Attribution & Control Case Study
documents.status: Public Evidence Edition — historical unresolved-provenance condition
terms: machine-readable audit trails for AI agents
documents.abstract: Preserves the historical account of later audit-style prompts and disputed billable execution after notice to the provider. It distinguishes operator evidence, support statements, product documentation, anecdotal context, and unresolved attribution.
claims: An empty visible task board does not establish the absence of every execution path.
The paper asks who or what created later prompts and what authority permitted billing.
Its original provenance uncertainty is materially updated by the later cross-system case study.
documents.boundary: Historical evidence state, not the final root-cause account. Later attribution must be linked explicitly rather than silently reconciling these versions.

documents.title: OBSERVATION BECAME BILLABLE EXECUTION
documents.subtitle: A Cross-System Automation, Agent Billing Attribution & Authority-Boundary Case Study
documents.status: Public Evidence Edition — revised causal attribution
documents.abstract: Updates the earlier Replit explanation with a provider-reported backend review and matching ChatGPT automation record. It reframes the issue around how recurring observation requests became billable agent input across connected systems.
claims: The revised record materially establishes prompt provenance according to the source's provider evidence and automation metadata.
The source corrects earlier restoration/queue explanations and records an approved refund.
Observation, execution, and spend authority remain separate control boundaries; authorization for one does not establish authorization for the others.
documents.boundary: A bounded revised incident account. Distinct spend-authorization and cross-system control questions remain unresolved; the catalog does not independently adjudicate provider or legal responsibility.

documents.title: THE PASSENGER
documents.subtitle: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Internal Modeling, the Vessel, Reality, Direction, and the Road a Life Appears to Offer
documents.abstract: Examines the author's reported experience of internal modeling through autobiography, comparative traditions, historical authorities, and a proposed Passenger/Vessel architecture. The name describes an observed experience without establishing its ultimate nature.
claims: The passenger is a name for the reported phenomenon, not an explanation or independently established entity.
The author separates remembered events from the later analytical model used to interpret them.
Structural comparison with traditions or historical figures is not presented as proof of shared ontology or diagnosis.
documents.boundary: First-person testimony, retrospective interpretation, comparative analysis, and an author-proposed lens remain distinct. The paper does not establish a soul, separate consciousness, or neurological subsystem.

related_evidence.before-you-name-the-machine: The existing statement explicitly names The Passenger in its account of the reality/consequence loop and bibliography.
related_evidence.governing-engines-journey: The Journey's September 29 continuation explicitly discusses The Passenger as a retrospective working model, not the historical premise from which MODE was deduced.

documents.title: A WALK THROUGH HUMANITY
documents.subtitle: Authority, Religion, Peoplehood, Empire, Persecution, Sovereignty, and the Human Chain to the Present
documents.abstract: Traces transformations of claimed, recognized, legal, effective, and contested authority across a historical chain. Its method distinguishes evidence categories and asks how authority is constructed, maintained, opposed, and transformed.
claims: Canonical order is not automatically chronological order; precedence alone does not establish truth.
The paper separates established, supported, contested, unresolved, and historically unknowable claims.
Historical method may investigate claims about supernatural authority without proving or disproving supernatural beings.
documents.boundary: Historical and comparative research with explicit evidence categories; this catalog does not independently revalidate its historical or contemporary sources. The v3.0 editorial note describes removal of redundant scaffolding without intentional loss of substantive findings.

related_evidence.the-passenger: Thematic comparison only: both supplied texts examine historical/religious authority, while The Passenger explicitly disclaims diagnosing historical figures. No citation or common causal lineage is asserted.
related_evidence.human-abstractions: Thematic comparison only: the historical work's claimed/legal/effective authority categories can be compared with Human Abstractions' distinction between consequential institutions and reality-level necessity. This does not imply either source proves the other.

documents.title: FOLLOW THE HARM
documents.subtitle: Proof, Power, and the Custody of Consequences in the Meta Youth-Safety Settlement
documents.abstract: Examines how reported human harm becomes evidence, public authority, bargaining leverage, and institutional value in the source's account of a Meta youth-safety settlement. It keeps victim outcomes separate from institutional outcomes and distinguishes legal evidence classes.
claims: An institutional enforcement outcome is not automatically an individual victim remedy.
The paper distinguishes adjudicated facts, allegations, settlement terms, reported facts, analysis, and unresolved questions.
Asymmetry between institutional and individual outcomes is not, by itself, proof of illegality or governance failure.
documents.boundary: Victim-centered investigative analysis, not legal advice or an independent adjudication by this repository. Source-reported settlement facts and external citations have not been reverified in this curation pass.

related_evidence.danger-zones: Danger Zones' Research lineage and section 10 explicitly identify Follow the Harm as its downstream case-study companion and distinguish preventive proof from post-harm evidence.

documents.title: FROM CREATION TO GOVERNED INTELLIGENCE
documents.subtitle: What We Built, What We Think May Be Emerging, What We Want, What We Reject, Where We Are, and What Comes Next
documents.version: Base Version 1.1; October Continuity Appendix F Version 1.0
documents.date: Base August 26, 2026; cumulative continuation through October 21, 2026
documents.status: Working Architectural Position / Architecture Position + Canonical Journey Record
documents.abstract: Preserves the cumulative Governing Engines lineage from creative production pressure toward governed intelligence, with dated continuations through October 21, 2026. It distinguishes historical events, architectural decisions, hypotheses, machine-state cutoffs, and unfinished work.
claims: Later continuations do not silently rewrite the August baseline or the September records.
The October continuation distinguishes internal ecosystem state, public MODE state, behavioral qualification, and Journey continuity as different records.
The supplied October account preserves scoped successes, failed diagnosis, open qualification gates, and the absence of proven production completion.
documents.boundary: A cumulative authorial continuity/lineage account, not an independently reproduced machine audit. Base and appendix versions/dates remain distinct; this stable canonical location will receive future appendices while Git preserves past editions.

related_evidence.the-passenger: The September 29 continuation explicitly discusses The Passenger and its retrospective role.
related_evidence.mode-machine-state-2026-09-14: The Journey preserves the September runtime/qualification lineage rather than rewriting it from later outcomes.
related_evidence.mode-machine-state-2026-10-21: Appendix F sections 3, 4 and 11 describe the same October cutoff and distinguish public machine-state records from continuity history; this is not independent corroboration.
related_evidence.mode: The Journey repeatedly separates MODE architecture/specification from implementation and evidence of runtime behavior.

documents.title: MODE LAST VERIFIED MACHINE STATE & TRACEABILITY RECORD
documents.subtitle: A reality-bounded snapshot of what had actually crossed from architecture into observed runtime
documents.status: Historical last-evidenced-state snapshot — not a live-machine claim
documents.abstract: Records the author's last supported MODE state at the September 14 cutoff, separating the September 3 architectural baseline from later provider-backed qualification evidence. It preserves observed runtime mechanisms alongside degraded behavior and unproven memory/build objectives.
claims: Existing documentation does not establish runtime operation, and missing visibility does not establish nonexistence.
The source reports a functioning provider path but failed behavior qualification in the scoped September run.
The source does not establish complete Understanding, runtime Reality Primacy integration, or successful end-to-end governed construction at that cutoff.
documents.boundary: Historical author-supplied evidence summary, not a current/live-machine claim or a fresh reproduction of MODE tests by this repository. Later snapshots do not retroactively change this dated evidence state.

related_evidence.mode: Section 10 lists the MODE Public Build Specification among this snapshot's evidence basis, while separating specifications from runtime truth.
related_evidence.mode-machine-state-2026-10-21: Same MODE evidence series at a later explicit cutoff; comparison preserves different machine states rather than claiming equivalent behavior or a controlled test.
related_evidence.governing-engines-journey: The Journey preserves September and October continuity as historically distinct records.

documents.title: MODE PUBLIC MACHINE STATE - MODE ONLY
documents.status: Current public MODE snapshot at the October 21, 2026 cutoff
documents.abstract: Describes MODE-only public state at the October 21 cutoff, with author-reported scoped learning, memory, and controlled self-inspection demonstrations alongside material failures and open gates. It separates engineering test results from behavioral evidence.
claims: The source reports bounded learning-expression, cross-thread-memory, and self-inspection/publication proofs rather than universal capabilities.
Generalized Learning, objective-driven Learning self-diagnosis, and end-to-end Objective Continuity remain unqualified or not demonstrated.
Failed, partial, inconclusive, and blocked behavioral records remain part of the evidence despite passing engineering suites.
documents.boundary: A public MODE-only, cutoff-specific author evidence record; its test counts and behavioral results were not rerun or independently verified in this repository-curation task. It is not the broader internal ecosystem record and does not claim production-ready autonomous execution.

related_evidence.mode: Same named MODE system as the public implementation specification, with the source expressly distinguishing implemented behavior from completeness and qualification.
related_evidence.mode-machine-state-2026-09-14: Dated snapshots in the same MODE series; the September snapshot remains historical rather than being overwritten.
related_evidence.governing-engines-journey: Appendix F sections 3 and 11 describe the October 21 cutoff and public-machine-state distinction; these shared author records do not constitute independent replication.

documents.title: MECHANISM PRIMACY
documents.abstract: This document establishes Mechanism Primacy as a foundational governing principle of Governing Engines.
claims: Mechanisms produce outcomes.
Outcomes do not explain themselves.
Understanding shall precede intervention.
documents.boundary: Foundational Governance Principle / Diagnostic Architecture / System Design Doctrine

related_evidence.governing-principles: Framework relationship: source identifies itself as a foundational governing principle.

documents.title: AI SYSTEM CONSTRUCTION METHOD
documents.abstract: The AI System Construction Method exists to transform an idea into a buildable, governable, testable, and deployable system.
claims: AI is not a system.
AI is a component.
The objective is system construction.
documents.boundary: System Construction Methodology. No source issue date is stated in the document; PDF creation metadata is not treated as its publication date.

related_evidence.operator-system-builder-development: Editorial methodology comparison: construction order and operator development; not a claim of identical works.
